summary: 光在海水中传播有限，低频声音却能沿深海声道抵达远方。原用于监测海下活动的接收系统后来被用于追踪鲸群，声波传播时间还能帮助研究者绘制海温变化。
logic: 比较光与声在水中的传播
从水下监听转向鲸类研究
用传播时间监测海温与气候

paragraphs.brief: 光线探洋为何不如观月
sentences: The oceans cover more than 70 per cent of the planet’s surface, yet until quite recently we knew less about their depths than about the surface of the Moon.
海洋占地球表面的70%以上，然而直到最近，我们对其深度的了解还不如对月球表面的了解。
The Moon has been far more accessible to study because astronomers have long been able to look at its surface, first with the naked eye and then with the telescope, both instruments that focus light.
月球研究的便利性要大得多，因为天文学家早就能够观察其表面，首先是肉眼，然后是望远镜，这两种仪器都是聚焦光的仪器。

Until the twentieth century, however, no instruments were available for the study of Earth’s oceans: light, which can travel trillions of kilometres through the vast vacuum of space, cannot penetrate very far in seawater.
然而，直到二十世纪，还没有可用于研究地球海洋的工具：光线能够穿越巨大的空间真空，穿越数万亿公里，但不能深入到海水中。
paragraphs.gist: 海洋虽覆盖地球七成以上面积，海底却曾比月面更难研究，因为能穿越广袤太空的光线穿不透深水，常规目视工具因而难以发挥作用。

paragraphs.brief: 水下钟声测出传播速度
sentences: It turns out that for penetrating water the best instrument is sound.
结果发现，对于渗入的水来说，最好的仪器是声音。
Curious investigators have long been fascinated by sound and the way it travels in water.
好奇的调查员早就对声音和它在水中行驶的方式着迷。

As early as 1490, the artist and scientist Leonardo da Vinci observed: ‘If you cause your ship to stop and place the head of a long tube in the water and place the outer extremity to your ear, you will hear ships at a great distance from you.’
早在 1490 年，艺术家兼科学家达·芬奇就观察到：“如果让船停下，把长管的一端放进水里，另一端贴到耳边，就能听到远处船只的声音。”
It was not until 1826 that two scientists, Colladon and Sturm, accurately measured the speed of sound in water.
直到1826年两位科学家科拉登和斯图尔姆精确测量了水中声音的速度
Using a long tube to listen under water (as da Vinci had suggested), they recorded how fast the sound of a submerged bell travelled across Lake Geneva in Switzerland.
他们按照达·芬奇的设想，用长管在水下听声，测出了瑞士日内瓦湖中一口水下钟的钟声在湖水中的传播速度。
What these investigators demonstrated was that water is an excellent medium for sound, transmitting it almost five times faster than its speed in air.
这些调查员证明，水是一个很好的声音媒介，传送速度几乎是空气速度的五倍。
paragraphs.gist: 达·芬奇曾建议借长管听水下声音，直到 1826 年两位研究者测量水中钟声传播所需时间，才准确算出水中声速接近空气中的五倍。

paragraphs.brief: 低频声沿深海声道远传
sentences: A number of factors influence how far sound travels under water and how long it lasts, including particles, salinity, temperature and pressure.
一些因素影响声音在水下流到多远，持续多长时间，包括颗粒、盐度、温度和压力。

Particles in seawater can reflect, scatter and absorb certain frequencies of sound, just as certain wavelengths of light may be reflected, scattered and absorbed by specific types of particles in the atmosphere.
海水中的粒子可以反射、散射和吸收某些声音频率，正如某些波长的光线可以被大气中特定种类的粒子反射、分散和吸收一样。

In 1943, Maurice Ewing and J. L. Worzel conducted an experiment to test the theory that low-frequency waves, which are less vulnerable than higher frequencies to scattering and absorption, should be able to travel great distances, if the sound source is placed correctly.
1943 年，莫里斯·尤因和 J. L. 沃泽尔设计实验检验一种推测：低频声波比高频声波较少受到散射和吸收，只要声源位置合适，就应能传播很远。
The researchers set off an underwater explosion and learned that it was detected easily by receivers 3,200 kilometres away.
研究人员发起了一次水下爆炸，并发现它很容易被接收器发现，距离3200公里。
In analysing the results of this test, they discovered a kind of ‘sound pipeline’, known as the ‘deep sound channel’.
分析这次实验时，他们发现了一条像“声音管道”一样的通路，即深海声道。
Sound introduced into this channel of water could travel thousands of kilometres with minimal loss of signal.
声音进入这一水层后，能传播数千公里，信号衰减极小。
paragraphs.gist: 海水颗粒、盐度等因素影响声音传播，而一次实验在三千二百公里外接收到水下信号，使研究者发现低频声可沿深海声道远传而损失极小。

paragraphs.brief: 军用水听器用来监听鲸声
sentences: The US Navy was quick to appreciate the usefulness of low-frequency sound and the deep sound channel.
美国海军很快认识到低频声和深海声道的用处。

They developed the Sound Surveillance System (SOSUS), which involved underwater microphones, called hydrophones, that were placed on the ocean bottom and connected by cables to on-shore processing centres.
他们开发了声音监测系统，其中包括水下麦克风，称为水下听筒，放在海底，电缆连接到岸上处理中心。
It was Christopher Clark of Cornell University who soon realised that SOSUS could be used to listen to whales.
康奈尔大学的克里斯托弗·克拉克不久后意识到SOSUS可以用来听鲸鱼的声音
Using a SOSUS receiver in the West Indies, he could hear whales that were 1,770 kilometres away.
利用西印度群岛的SOSUS接收器他可以听到1,770公里外的鲸鱼声
paragraphs.gist: 美国海军用海底水听器建立声音监测系统，康奈尔大学的克拉克发现它还可监听鲸类，在西印度群岛便听到一千七百七十公里外的鲸声。

paragraphs.brief: 同时追踪多鲸并辨别叫声
sentences: Whales are the biggest of Earth’s creatures, yet these animals are also remarkably elusive.
鲸鱼是地球上最大的生物，然而这些动物也非常难以捉摸。
Scientists wishing to observe blue whales must simply wait in their ships for the whales to surface.
希望观察蓝鲸的科学家必须在船上等待鲸鱼浮出水面
A few whales have been tracked briefly in the wild in this way but not for very great distances, and much about them remains unknown.
少数鲸鱼在野外被以这种方式短暂跟踪，但距离不远，关于它们的许多情况仍然不明。
But by using SOSUS, scientists can track the whales and position them on a map.
但是通过使用SOSUS，科学家可以追踪鲸鱼并将其定位在地图上。
Moreover, they can track not just one whale at a time, but many creatures simultaneously.
此外，它们不仅可以一次跟踪一只鲸鱼，而且可以同时跟踪许多生物。

They can also learn to distinguish whale calls; researchers have detected changes in the calls of finback whales as the seasons change, and have found that blue whales in different regions of the Pacific Ocean have different calls.
研究者还能辨别不同鲸类的叫声，已发现长须鲸的叫声随季节变化，而太平洋不同海区的蓝鲸也有各自的叫声。
paragraphs.gist: 海上观察者往往只能短暂看到上浮的蓝鲸，而水声系统可同时定位多头鲸，还能发现不同季节或不同海区鲸类叫声的变化。

paragraphs.brief: 以声音传播时间绘制海温图
sentences: SOSUS has also proved instrumental in obtaining information crucial to our understanding of climate.
SOSUS也证明在获取对我们了解气候至关重要的信息方面起了重要作用。

The system has enabled researchers to begin making ocean-temperature measurements on a global scale, measurements that are key to understanding the workings of heat transfer between the ocean and the atmosphere.
该系统使研究人员能够开始在全球范围内进行海洋温度测量，这些测量是了解海洋和大气之间热量转移工作的关键。
The ocean plays an enormous role in determining air temperature — the heat capacity in only the upper few metres of ocean is thought to be equal to all of the heat in the entire atmosphere.
海洋对气温的影响极大，人们认为，仅表层几米海水所能容纳的热量，就可与整个大气层所含的热量相比。
For sound waves travelling horizontally in the ocean, speed is largely a function of temperature.
声波在海洋中水平移动速度主要是温度的函数
Thus, the travel time of a wave of sound between two points is a sensitive indicator of the average temperature along its path.
因此，两个点之间的声波的穿梭时间是其沿途平均温度的敏感指标。
Transmitting sound in numerous directions through the deep sound channel can give scientists measurements spanning vast areas of the globe.
沿深海声道向多个方向发射声音，便可在全球广阔海域取得测量数据。

Thousands of sound paths in the ocean can be pieced together into a map of global ocean temperatures, and by repeating measurements along the same paths over time, scientists can track changes in temperature over months or years.
海洋中的数千条声音路径可以拼凑成全球海洋温度的地图，通过沿同一条路径的重复测量，科学家可以跟踪几个月或几年的温度变化。
paragraphs.gist: 海水温度会影响声波传播速度，研究者把许多声路的传播时间拼成全球海温图，并通过在同一路线上复测来追踪长期变化。

paragraphs.brief: 让水听器成为天然雨量计
sentences: Researchers are also using other acoustic techniques to monitor climate.
研究人员还利用其他声学技术监测气候。
Oceanographer Jeff Nystuen, for example, has explored the use of sound to measure rainfall over the ocean.
例如，海洋学家Jeff Nystuen探讨了如何利用声音测量海洋降雨量。
Monitoring changing global rainfall patterns will contribute to understanding major climate change as well as the weather phenomenon known as El Niño.
监测不断变化的全球降雨模式将有助于了解重大的气候变化以及被称为厄尔尼诺的天气现象。
Since 1985, Nystuen has used hydrophones to listen to rain over the ocean, acoustically measuring not only the rainfall rate but also the rainfall type, ranging from drizzle to thunderstorms.
自1985年以来，Nystuen一直使用水听器来听大海的降雨，声学上不仅测量降雨率，而且测量降雨类型，从喷雨到雷暴不等。
By using the sound of rain under water as a ‘natural’ rain gauge, the measurement of rainfall over the oceans will become available to climatologists.
气候学家将利用水下雨水的声音作为“自然”雨量表，测量海洋降雨量。
In this way, modern society continues to benefit from the investigations of those who, like Leonardo da Vinci, pursued the answers to some basic questions of nature.
这样，现代社会继续受益于对象莱昂纳多·达芬奇这样的人的调查，他们寻求对一些基本自然问题的答案。
paragraphs.gist: 尼斯图恩把水听器当作天然雨量计，以雨滴落海的声音测降雨，从而为研究海洋上空的降水分布和全球气候变化提供资料。

items.en: examples of things that affect the distance sound can travel in water
items.zh: 举例说明哪些因素影响声音在水中的传播
items.why: C段列出颗粒物、盐度、温度和压力，都是影响水下声音传播距离的因素。

items.en: details of the connection between ocean temperatures and climate
items.zh: 海洋温度和气候之间联系的细节
items.why: F段用海洋储热量与大气作比较，解释海温的微小变化为何对气候很重要。

items.en: details of ways in which light and sound are similar
items.zh: 描述光和声音在传播上有哪些相似之处
items.why: 海水中的颗粒会反射、散射或吸收一定频率的声波，作者将它与光波相似的传播特征作比较。

items.en: a reference to a long-term study of different types of weather
items.zh: 提及对不同类型天气的长期研究
items.why: 研究从1985年起持续用水听器记录海面降雨，区分毛毛雨和雷暴等类型，同时满足“长期”和“不同天气”。

items.en: In the past, it was easier for scientists to study the Moon than the oceans.
items.zh: 过去，科学家们研究月球比研究海洋更容易。
items.why: 月面长期可用肉眼和望远镜观测，深海却难以用光探测，所以昔日研究月球更容易。

items.en: Techniques for investigating the Moon are the same as techniques for researching the ocean.
items.zh: 月球研究技术与海洋研究技术相同。
items.why: 研究月面可借助光，光在海水中却难以深入；深海探测用到声学，两者的方法有别。

items.en: Measuring temperature changes in the ocean using sound is more time-consuming than other methods.
items.zh: 使用声音测量海洋温度变化比其他方法更费时。
items.why: 重复声学测量可以跟踪海温变化，文章没有比较这种方法与其他方法各花多少时间。

items.en: Hydrophones can distinguish different kinds of rain.
items.zh: 水听器能分辨出不同类型的降雨。
items.why: 水听器既能测量降雨量，也能区分毛毛雨到雷暴等雨型。

items.en: According to the passage, who conducted research into the rate at which sound travels in water?
items.zh: 根据本文，谁研究了声音在水中的传播速度？

items.en: According to the passage, who conducted research into the distances certain types of sound waves travel in water?
items.zh: 根据本文，谁研究了某些声波在水中能传播多远？

clauses: “that for penetrating water the best instrument is sound”补足 turns 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 turns 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

In 1943, Maurice Ewing and J. L. Worzel conducted an experiment to test the theory that low-frequency waves, which are less vulnerable than higher frequencies to scattering and absorption, should be able to travel great distances, ….
连接词 if 引出“if the sound source is placed correctly”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
